audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Akshan all seven stages, which the packet itself flags as a defect ('Nautilus wins 80% but the chart gives Akshan 5/7 stages vs 1') and which contradicts the prose sitting beside it: whys[0] says Nautilus's passive root edges the level-1 auto trade, and whys[6], spikes[3] and the late block all say Nautilus walks him down with two items.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is Skill/Akshan/Akshan/Akshan/Akshan/Akshan/Nautilus, which matches the prose exactly. Only rows 0 and 6 were wrong; rows 1-5 genuinely belong to Akshan and stay.
audit.corrected: Row 0 set to Skill and row 6 to Nautilus in BOTH layers as matched pairs, with ratings raised from 2/10 to 5/10 and 3/10 to 6/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 3 and level 6 were named as Akshan spikes with no cooldowns attached, and the level-6 spike was built on 'revive-trades' — Going Rogue's resurrection.
audit.why: Going Rogue only resurrects allies when Akshan kills a champion who is marked as a Scoundrel for having killed one of his allies. That is not a lane-phase resource against a solo Nautilus, so a spike built on it is misleading. The real level-6 spike is Comeuppance: 100s at rank 1, damage scaling off the target's missing health, which is exactly what punishes a Nautilus who commits and does not finish.
audit.corrected: Level-6 spike rebuilt on Comeuppance's 100s cooldown and missing-health scaling; level-3 spike now carries Heroic Swing's 18s rank-1 cooldown and its terrain requirement.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fields said Akshan 'swings off your terrain Q' — treating Dredge Line as if it creates terrain for him to grapple. It does not. Riot's text: colliding with terrain pulls NAUTILUS toward it. The derived 'terrain' flag on Nautilus's Q misfires here.
audit.why: The decisive interaction is the reverse of what the page said: Heroic Swing needs existing terrain to anchor, so the lane walls are his escape route and Nautilus's Q gives him nothing. The mirror audit reached the same conclusion from Akshan's side ('walls are his approach route, not your cover').
audit.corrected: Every 'terrain Q' grapple claim replaced with the real rule — he anchors to lane walls, so fight him in the open — and the abilities are named throughout: Heroic Swing, Avengerang, Comeuppance, Staggering Blow, Dredge Line, Riptide.

edits.before: His E grapple swings off any terrain to reset the angle, so your Q-pull and E slow chase empty air while his Q pokes you.
edits.after: Avengerang damages going out and coming back, and its range extends off every enemy it clips, so he wins the level-2 poke war.

edits.after: Heroic Swing needs a wall to anchor — beside terrain he swings out of every link of your chain.

edits.after: Depth Charge is undodgeable, but Comeuppance stores bullets off your missing health and kills you if you don't finish in the lockup.

edits.before: Akshan gets his E grapple online — now he swings off your terrain Q and kites your whole CC chain; your favored auto-trade window slams shut.
edits.after: Heroic Swing comes online — anywhere beside a wall he swings clear of your CC chain, and it is back in 18s; your free auto-trade window shuts.

edits.before: His Q poke plus camouflage passive let him chunk and reset on you; your R hooks him but he revive-trades and out-DPSes the lockup if you don't one-shot.
edits.after: Comeuppance lands at 100s and its stored bullets scale off your missing health; your R hooks him out of a swing, but he out-DPSes the lockup unless a jungler follows in.

edits.after: Use Heroic Swing off the lane walls to kite every link of your CC chain

edits.before: Poke you down with Q and reset aggression with his camouflage passive
edits.after: Poke you down with Avengerang — its range extends off every enemy it hits

edits.before: Level 1 is the one moment this lane is yours — he has no E grapple yet, so my first auto roots him with passive and a clean Q lands a stun-pull he can't swing out of. Step up and threaten that the instant he walks to a minion. The catch: I have to hit Q ON HIM, not the wall, or it just yanks me forward into his Q poke. Once he hits Level 3 and his E comes online he grapples off any terrain near him and the auto-trades stop being free.
edits.after: Level 1 is the one moment this lane is yours — he has no Heroic Swing yet, so Staggering Blow roots on my first attack and a clean Dredge Line lands a pull he can't swing out of. Step up and threaten that the instant he walks to a minion. The catch: I have to hit Q ON HIM, not the wall, or it just yanks me forward into Avengerang. Once Heroic Swing comes online he grapples off any wall near him and the auto-trades stop being free.

edits.before: From Levels 3 to 6 he runs the lane on his terms — E swings reset his angle so my Q-pull and E slow whiff into empty space, and his Q chunks me every time I walk up to farm. At 6 my R is undodgeable and hooks him out of a swing, but he'll camouflage-reset, revive-trade, and out-DPS the lockup unless I land R+E+passive perfectly and a jungler follows. Don't flop forward on a terrain Q hoping to reach him; bait his E cooldown and only commit R when his grapple is down.
edits.after: From Levels 3 to 6 he runs the lane on his terms — Heroic Swing resets his angle so my Q-pull and Riptide slow whiff into empty space, and Avengerang chunks me every time I walk up to farm. At 6 my R is undodgeable and hooks him out of a swing, but Comeuppance answers off my missing health and out-DPSes the lockup unless I land R+E+passive perfectly and a jungler follows. Don't flop forward on a terrain Q hoping to reach him; bait the 18 seconds of Heroic Swing and only commit R when it is down.

edits.before: - Akshan Heroic Swing: matchup-defining — His dash + camera swing escape. Engage when it's down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Akshan Heroic Swing: 18s at rank 1 and it must anchor to a wall — fight him away from terrain. - Comeuppance: 100s, and it fires off your missing health. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

edits.before: His dash + camera swing escape. Engage when it's down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: He needs a wall to anchor Heroic Swing, and it is down 18s at rank 1. Fight in the open lane.

edits.before: Track Akshan's Heroic Swing: His dash + camera swing escape. Engage when it's down. When it is down — Hook + passive root chain.
edits.after: Track Heroic Swing: it must anchor to terrain and is down 18s at rank 1. When down — hook, passive root, Riptide slow.

notes: Nautilus's Dredge Line carries a derived 'terrain' flag that Riot's description does not support — the Q does not create terrain, it pulls Nautilus to terrain it hits. Three fields had been written as though Akshan could grapple off a Nautilus Q; all three are corrected, and the mirror audit agrees. 'Dirty Fighting' is Akshan's real passive name (a suspectNames false positive in the mirror's packet). NOT asserted, because the kit text does not confirm it: whether Depth Charge's knockup interrupts an in-progress Heroic Swing (the late block already claims 'R to cancel his escape swing' — I left that string alone rather than delete or strengthen it), and whether Comeuppance's bullet-storing is a channel that CC can break. Sample is 15 games at 80%, so the win rate is thin evidence; the chart change is justified by the prose and the packet chart, not the win rate alone.
